headline: Access strength lifts sales; margin squeeze cuts EPS outlook
summary_short: Oshkosh grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 6.7% y/y to $2.92B on Access segment strength, but operating income fell 16.6% to $243.2M as unfavorable mix and tariff-driven costs outweighed pricing gains, and diluted EPS fell 7.6% to $2.92.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.7% y/y to $2.92B, led by Access segment volume and pricing, but operating income fell 16.6% to $243.2M as unfavorable sales mix, tariff-driven material costs, and higher manufacturing overhead outweighed pricing gains; gross margin compressed 270bps to 16.5%. Net income fell 10.5% to $183.2M and diluted EPS fell 7.6% to $2.92, partly cushioned by a lower effective tax rate (16.9% vs 24.1%) tied to a foreign anti-hybrid tax benefit. Consolidated backlog rose 3.7% y/y to $14.75B. The company cut FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance to $10.50 (from $10.90) on slower municipal fire-apparatus ramp-up, while raising full-year sales guidance to ~$11.2B (from ~$11.0B); adjusted EPS guide is $11.00.

drivers.explanation: Consolidated sales rose 6.7% on higher Access equipment volume and improved pricing, but operating income fell 16.6% as unfavorable sales mix, tariff-driven material costs, and higher manufacturing overhead more than offset the pricing and volume gains.
Higher sales volume, largely in the Access segment, added $87 million; improved pricing added $68 million.
Gross profit fell $44.2 million as margin compression from unfavorable mix and higher material costs outweighed the benefit of higher sales volume and pricing.
Margin fell 270 basis points: unfavorable sales mix (200bps), higher tariff-related material costs (170bps), and higher manufacturing overhead (80bps) outweighed a 170bp pricing benefit.

Operating income fell on higher material costs ($55M), unfavorable sales mix ($52M), higher manufacturing overhead ($25M), and higher warranty costs ($10M), partly offset by improved pricing ($68M) and the gross-margin benefit of higher volume ($23M).
Operating margin fell 240 basis points as operating income declined 16.6% while revenue grew 6.7% -- cost growth outpaced the topline gain.

Net income fell as lower operating income was only partly offset by a lower effective tax rate (16.9% vs 24.1%), which included a $15.7 million discrete benefit from an expiring foreign anti-hybrid tax matter.
EPS declined with net income, partly cushioned by a smaller diluted share count; share repurchases over the trailing twelve months benefited per-share results by $0.09 versus a year ago.
